title: Introduction to Quarters Using Rectangular Cut-outs
subject: Mathematics

steps.title: Welcome!
steps.purpose: Greet the child and set emotional tone for learning about one quarter (1/4)
steps.owlText: Hello friend! Today we are going to learn about quarters! A quarter is one of four equal parts. Are you ready?
steps.studentText: Today we learn about quarters. A quarter is one of four equal parts!

media.altText: Owl teacher waving hello with a rectangle divided into 4 equal parts
media.fallbackText: Hello friend! Today we learn about quarters.

steps.title: Our Mission
steps.purpose: Tell the child what they will learn about one quarter (1/4)
steps.studentText: Today you will learn what a quarter is. A quarter means one of four equal parts of something whole.

steps.title: Think First!
steps.purpose: Activate prior knowledge about equal parts and sharing
steps.owlText: Before we start, think about this: If you have one cake and want to share it fairly with 3 friends (4 people total), how would you cut it so everyone gets the same amount?
steps.studentText: How would you share one cake fairly with 3 friends? Think about it!

media.altText: A whole cake with a question mark above it
media.fallbackText: Think about sharing one cake fairly with 3 friends.

steps.title: Learn It
steps.purpose: Teach the core concept of one quarter (1/4)
steps.owlText: When we cut something into four equal parts, each part is called a quarter. Look at this rectangle. I will fold it into four equal parts. Each part is one quarter. We write it as 1/4.
steps.studentText: A quarter means one of four equal parts. When you fold a paper into four equal parts, each part is one quarter. We write: 1/4

media.altText: A rectangle being folded into 4 equal parts. One part is shaded. Shows 1/4.
media.caption: One quarter. We write it as 1/4.
media.fallbackText: A rectangle divided into 4 equal parts. One part is shaded. This is one quarter. We write it as 1/4.

steps.title: Real Life Connection
steps.purpose: Connect one quarter (1/4) to everyday life with real examples
steps.owlText: We see quarters every day! When you cut a cake into four equal slices, each slice is one quarter. When you fold a paper into four equal parts, each part is one quarter. Quarters are all around us!
steps.studentText: We see quarters every day! When you cut a cake into four equal slices, each slice is one quarter. Quarters are all around us!

media.altText: A cake cut into 4 equal slices. A paper folded into 4 equal parts.
media.caption: Quarters in real life: cake and paper folding.
media.fallbackText: A cake cut into 4 equal slices. Each slice is one quarter.

steps.title: Watch and Learn
steps.purpose: Show a worked example of identifying one quarter (1/4)
steps.owlText: Let me show you. This rectangle is divided into 4 equal parts. One part is shaded. The shaded part is one quarter of the whole rectangle. We write it as 1/4. All four parts are the same size — that is what makes them equal.
steps.studentText: Look at this rectangle. It is divided into 4 equal parts. One part is shaded. The shaded part is one quarter of the whole rectangle. We write: 1/4. All four parts are the same size.

media.altText: A rectangle divided into 4 equal parts. One part is shaded. Arrow points to shaded part labeled 1/4.
media.caption: The shaded part is one quarter. We write: 1/4
media.fallbackText: A rectangle divided into 4 equal parts. One part is shaded. This is one quarter. We write: 1/4.

steps.title: Your Turn!
steps.purpose: Child practices identifying one quarter (1/4) — different from Quick Check
steps.owlText: Now it is your turn! Look at these two shapes. One shape is divided into four equal parts. The other is not. Which shape shows quarters? Tap the correct one.
steps.studentText: Which shape is divided into 4 equal parts? Tap the shape that shows quarters.

media.altText: Two shapes side by side. Shape A: rectangle divided into 4 equal parts. Shape B: rectangle divided into 4 unequal parts.
media.fallbackText: Two rectangles. One has 4 equal parts. One has 4 unequal parts. Which shows quarters?

interaction.question: Which shape shows one quarter (1/4)?
interaction.feedbackCorrect: Yes! Shape A has 4 equal parts with 1 shaded. That is one quarter!
interaction.feedbackIncorrect: Look for a shape with 4 equal parts. One of those parts should be shaded. That shows one quarter.

steps.title: Quick Check!
steps.purpose: Test understanding of one quarter (1/4) — fraction identification
steps.owlText: Quick check! This circle is divided into 4 equal parts. One part is shaded. What fraction is shaded? Choose the correct answer.
steps.studentText: This circle is divided into 4 equal parts. One part is shaded. What fraction is shaded?

media.altText: A circle divided into 4 equal parts. One part is shaded.
media.fallbackText: A circle divided into 4 equal parts. One part is shaded.

interaction.question: This rectangle is divided into 4 equal parts. One part is shaded. What fraction is shaded?
interaction.feedbackCorrect: Yes! One out of four equal parts is one quarter. We write it as 1/4. Excellent!
interaction.feedbackIncorrect: Count the equal parts. There are 4. One part is shaded. That's one quarter (1/4).

steps.title: Think About Your Learning
steps.purpose: Help the child reflect on what they learned
steps.owlText: You did great today! Think about what you learned. What is a quarter? When something is divided into four equal parts, each part is one quarter.
steps.studentText: What did you learn about quarters today? A quarter means one of four equal parts.

interaction.question: How do you feel about quarters today?

steps.title: You Did It!
steps.owlText: Wonderful! You learned about quarters today. A quarter means one of four equal parts. You can find quarters in cake, paper, and many things around you. Keep practicing!
steps.studentText: You learned about quarters! A quarter is one of four equal parts. Look for quarters around you!

media.altText: Celebration with stars and a badge that says 'I know quarters!'
media.fallbackText: Wonderful! You learned about quarters today!
